chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who prays and does not take his hands out of his garment, so he said: 'If he takes his hands out, it is good; and if he does not take them out, there is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: Is it mandatory to take hands out of the garment when raising them during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the permissibility of varying methods for raising hands (raf' al-yadayn) during prayer, establishing that keeping hands within the garment is valid though less preferred. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of flexibility in non-obligatory acts of worship, where the core validity of the prayer is not compromised by minor deviations in ritual etiquette. This ruling underscores the balance between following the Sunnah and avoiding unnecessary hardship in daily worship practices.
